orbitSummary: Medium Earth orbit, about 20,000-23,000 km up, 12-14 hour period, part of a constellation of 24-30 satellites.
description: Redundant critical units, 12+ year life, harsh radiation environment.

subsystems.name: Structure & Mechanisms
subsystems.description: The bus carries ~700 kg of hardware through launch and holds the antennas, sensors and wings in precise alignment for 12+ years.

slots.name: Primary structure
slots.why: Honeycomb panels form the box; the Earth deck carries the navigation antenna.

variants.name: Aluminium honeycomb bus
variants.description: Aluminium skins on aluminium honeycomb: proven, easy to build.

variants.name: Carbon-fibre honeycomb bus
variants.description: Carbon-fibre skins: lighter and more thermally stable, more expensive.

slots.name: Launch adapter / separation system
slots.why: Bolts the satellite to the rocket and releases it in orbit. Navigation satellites are often launched several at a time.

variants.name: Clamp-band adapter ring
variants.description: A clamp band holds the ring until pyrotechnic bolts release it.

slots.name: Wing hold-down & release + hinges
slots.why: Holds the folded wings against the bus during launch; spring hinges unfold them after release.

subsystems.name: Navigation Payload
subsystems.description: The mission: broadcast extremely precise time and orbit data so receivers on Earth can compute their position. Everything starts from the atomic clocks.

slots.name: Atomic clocks
slots.why: Navigation accuracy comes from time accuracy: 1 ns of clock error is about 30 cm of position error.

variants.name: 2 rubidium + 2 hydrogen maser
variants.description: Masers are the most stable; rubidium clocks are compact backups.

variants.name: 4 rubidium clocks
variants.description: Lighter and cheaper, slightly less stable.

slots.name: Clock monitoring & control unit
slots.why: Compares the clocks and switches to a backup if one drifts.

slots.name: Navigation signal generator
slots.why: Builds the ranging codes and the navigation message from the clock signal.

slots.name: Frequency generation & up-conversion
slots.why: Turns the clock's reference into the L-band carrier frequencies.

slots.name: L-band power amplifiers
slots.why: Make the signal strong enough to be received on Earth from ~23,000 km.

variants.name: Solid-state amplifiers
variants.description: Rugged, efficient enough, gentle failure modes.

variants.name: Travelling-wave tube amplifiers
variants.description: More efficient at high power, heavier power supplies.

slots.name: Output multiplexer
slots.why: Combines the signals of all bands into the antenna.

slots.name: L-band navigation antenna
slots.why: Broadcasts to the whole visible Earth with a shaped beam.

variants.name: Helix array
variants.description: Array of helical elements on the Earth deck.

parameters.label: Number of helix elements
parameters.help: More elements give a better-shaped beam.

slots.name: Mission uplink receiver + antenna
slots.why: Receives fresh orbit and clock corrections from the ground every few hours.

slots.name: Laser retroreflector array
slots.why: Corner cubes that bounce ground laser pulses straight back: an independent, centimetre-level check of the orbit. Strongly recommended.

slots.name: Search & rescue transponder
slots.why: Relays distress beacons from ships, aircraft and people to rescue centres.

subsystems.name: Electrical Power (EPS)
subsystems.description: Sun-tracking wings power the satellite; batteries cover eclipse seasons, when the Earth's shadow crosses the orbit for up to about an hour per revolution.

slots.name: Solar wings
slots.why: Main power source. Folded for launch, unfolded in orbit.

parameters.label: Panel length
parameters.help: Longer panels = more area = more power.

parameters.label: Panel length
parameters.help: Longer panels = more area = more power.

slots.name: Solar array drive mechanisms
slots.why: Turn each wing about its axis so the cells keep facing the Sun.

variants.name: 2 drive mechanisms
variants.description: Stepper-motor drives with slip rings carrying the power.

slots.name: Li-ion battery
slots.why: Supplies power during eclipses.

variants.name: 5 kWh battery
variants.description: More reserve for longer eclipses and failures.

slots.name: Power conditioning & distribution unit
slots.why: Regulates the bus voltage, charges the battery, switches and protects every load.

slots.name: Release-actuator electronics
slots.why: Fires the hold-down release devices at the right time.

subsystems.name: On-board Computer (C&DH)
subsystems.description: Command and data handling. Every critical unit has a backup, because a single failure must not lose a satellite that people navigate by.

slots.name: On-board computers
slots.why: Run the modes, attitude control and fault handling.

variants.name: 2 on-board computers
variants.description: Cold-redundant pair: one on, one off.

slots.name: Mass memory
slots.why: Stores telemetry and payload housekeeping.

slots.name: Remote interface units
slots.why: Connect the computer to sensors, heaters and actuators.

slots.name: Data bus
slots.why: The redundant network between all units.

subsystems.name: Communications (TT&C)
subsystems.description: S-band link for commands, telemetry and ranging. Unlike LEO, a MEO satellite stays in view of a ground station for hours.

slots.name: S-band transponders
slots.why: Receive commands, send telemetry, and return ranging tones to measure distance.

slots.name: Omni antennas
slots.why: Two antennas (Earth side and space side) so contact works in any attitude.

slots.name: RF switches, diplexers, filters
slots.why: Route signals between transponders and antennas.

slots.name: Command encryption unit
slots.why: Navigation is critical infrastructure: only authenticated commands are accepted.

subsystems.name: Attitude Control (ADCS)
subsystems.description: Keeps the navigation antenna on the centre of the Earth and the wings on the Sun. Earth's magnetic field is too weak at MEO for magnetorquers, so thrusters unload the wheels.

slots.name: Earth sensors
slots.why: Measure roll and pitch relative to the Earth.

slots.name: Sun sensors
slots.why: Point the wings, steer yaw, find the Sun in safe mode.

slots.name: Gyros / inertial measurement unit
slots.why: Measure rotation rates.

slots.name: Reaction wheels
slots.why: Precise attitude control; four in a pyramid so any three can do the job.

parameters.label: Flywheel radius
parameters.help: Bigger wheels store more momentum, so thrusters unload them less often.

slots.name: Star trackers
slots.why: Higher pointing accuracy, especially for precise yaw steering.

subsystems.name: Thermal Control
subsystems.description: Removes heat from the amplifiers and keeps the clocks extremely stable, because their frequency shifts with temperature.

slots.name: Radiators
slots.why: Mirror-tile panels that radiate heat to space; placed on faces that see little Sun.

slots.name: Thermally stable clock panel
slots.why: An isolated, tightly heated panel for the clocks.

slots.name: Heaters + thermistors
slots.why: Keep every unit within its limits, especially in eclipse.

slots.name: Multi-layer insulation
slots.why: The blanket you see on the bus: insulates everything that is not a radiator.

slots.name: Heat pipes
slots.why: Move heat sideways from hot units to the radiators.
slots.conditionText: your amplifiers dissipate hundreds of watts

slots.name: Radiation shielding
slots.why: MEO crosses the outer Van Allen belt: radiation-tolerant parts plus extra shielding around sensitive units.

subsystems.name: Propulsion
subsystems.description: Corrects the orbit after launch, keeps the satellite in its slot in the constellation, unloads the wheels, and moves it to a disposal orbit at end of life.

slots.name: Hydrazine tank
slots.why: Propellant for the whole 12+ year life.

variants.name: Hydrazine tank (blowdown)
variants.description: Pressurant gas shares the tank and pushes the propellant out.

parameters.label: Propellant load
parameters.help: Mass of hydrazine loaded before launch.

slots.name: Thrusters
slots.why: Small monopropellant thrusters in two independent branches.

slots.name: Valves, filters, pressure sensors
slots.why: Isolate, protect and measure the propellant system.
